description: Conservative retired client matched to money market fund — all rules pass
client_narrative: Maria Santos is 67 years old and recently retired. She receives a monthly pension of about 2,100 euros. She has 80,000 euros sitting in a savings account and is looking to invest 50,000 euros of that for approximately 2 years. Her entire investment history consists of fixed-term bank deposits and standard savings accounts — she has never owned a stock, fund, or any product beyond basic bank savings instruments. She describes herself as very conservative: 'I cannot afford to lose what I have saved. Losing any portion of this money would seriously affect my finances. My only goal is capital preservation.'
product_narrative: The product is a short-term money market fund investing exclusively in high-quality, short-duration eurozone sovereign and agency instruments rated at least A-. The fund is registered as a UCITS, listed on Euronext Amsterdam, publishes a KID, and uses no leverage or derivatives of any kind. Capital preservation is the primary objective. The recommended minimum investment period is one year.
